page: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The CPU allocation is dedicated, supported by an L3 cache of 32 MB, L2 cache of 0.5 MB, and L1d cache of 32 KB. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, includes a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, and does not bundle local storage or GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and computational capabilities. The server achieves top 25% performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as PassMark CPU, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Memory performance is split; cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth falls in the top 25%, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths reside in the middle 50%. In software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, the instance registers strong scores in the top 25%. However, text processing and gzip/bzip3 decompression tasks perform in the average middle 50% tier.

For database and transactional workloads, the c6a.16xlarge demonstrates strong performance, as evidenced by its top 25% ranking in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations. Large language model inference speeds are strong for small models but drop to average for medium and large models. Given its dedicated compute resources, high core density, and DDR4 memory configuration, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, database operations, and small-scale LLM inference.
